knowledge:
- key_parameters: type=in convertASpli, specifies the count type ("gene", "bin", or "junction") ;; method=in calculateOffsets, specifies the normalization method ("TMM" or "geommean" for expression; "AS" or "proportion" for splicing) ;; aggregation=in calculateOffsets, specifies the rowData column used to aggregate feature counts ("locus" for bins; "symbol" or "ASpliCluster" for junctions) ;; mergeGeneASpli=in calculateOffsets, logical indicating whether to merge gene and ASpli cluster annotations for junctions ;; method=in saseRfindEncodingDim, specifies the method to choose the number of latent factors ("GD" for Gavish and Donoho threshold, or "DAE" for denoising autoencoder) ;; analysis=in saseRfit, specifies the analysis type ("AE" for aberrant expression, "AS" for aberrant splicing) ;; fit=in saseRfit, specifies the parameter estimation method ("fast" for overdispersed quadratic mean-variance relationship, or "edgeR") ;; padjust=in saseRfit, specifies the p-value adjustment method (e.g., "BH")
- alternatives: fit = "edgeR" in saseRfit instead of "fast" (can be used when the number of confounders is small, though no performance increase is expected) ;; method = "DAE" in saseRfindEncodingDim instead of "GD" (slower, but has similar performance) ;; Using conventional tools like DESeq2 or edgeR with adapted offsets for differential usage/splicing analysis instead of the full saseR aberrant pipeline
- when_to_use: Appropriate for bulk RNA-seq datasets, especially in the context of rare Mendelian disorders and outlier detection (aberrant expression and splicing). Also useful for performing differential usage/splicing analysis using standard tools (DESeq2/edgeR) with custom offsets.
- pitfalls: For aberrant expression, filter features before calculating offsets. For aberrant splicing, calculate offsets before filtering features. ;; In DESeq2/edgeR differential usage analysis, offsets cannot be equal to 0; any 0 offsets (and corresponding counts) must be adjusted (e.g., set to 1) before running the models. ;; The binGenome function can take a while to run.

workflows.name: aberrant_expression_analysis
workflows.intent: Detect aberrant gene expression from BAM files and GTF annotation.
workflows.stages: 1. Convert GTF to TxDb and extract genomic features using binGenome ;; 2. Count reads from BAM files using BamtoAspliCounts ;; 3. Extract gene counts using convertASpli ;; 4. Define design formula in metadata ;; 5. Filter low-count genes using filterByExpr ;; 6. Calculate normalization offsets using calculateOffsets ;; 7. Estimate latent confounders using saseRfindEncodingDim ;; 8. Fit the regression model and calculate p-values using saseRfit
workflows.code:
gtfFileName <- ASpli::aspliExampleGTF()
BAMFiles <- ASpli::aspliExampleBamList()
targets <- data.frame( 
  row.names = paste0('Sample',c(1:12)),
  bam = BAMFiles,
  f1 = rep("A",12),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
genomeTxDb <- txdbmaker::makeTxDbFromGFF(gtfFileName)
features <- binGenome(genomeTxDb, logTo = NULL)
ASpliSE <- BamtoAspliCounts(
                    features = features,
                    targets = targets,
                    minReadLength = 100,
                    libType = "SE",
                    BPPARAM = MulticoreParam(1L)
                    )
SEgenes <- convertASpli(ASpliSE, type = "gene")
metadata(SEgenes)$design <- ~1
filtergenes <- filterByExpr(SEgenes)
SEgenes <- SEgenes[filtergenes,]
SEgenes <- calculateOffsets(SEgenes, method = "TMM")
SEgenes <- saseRfindEncodingDim(SEgenes, method = "GD")
SEgenes <- saseRfit(SEgenes,
                    analysis = "AE",
                    padjust = "BH",
                    fit = "fast")

workflows.name: aberrant_splicing_analysis
workflows.intent: Detect aberrant splicing (at bin or junction level) from BAM files and GTF annotation.
workflows.stages: 1. Convert GTF to TxDb and extract genomic features using binGenome ;; 2. Count reads from BAM files using BamtoAspliCounts ;; 3. Extract bin or junction counts using convertASpli ;; 4. Define design formula in metadata ;; 5. Calculate splicing offsets using calculateOffsets (before filtering) ;; 6. Filter low-count features using filterByExpr ;; 7. Estimate latent confounders using saseRfindEncodingDim ;; 8. Fit the regression model and calculate p-values using saseRfit
workflows.code:
gtfFileName <- ASpli::aspliExampleGTF()
BAMFiles <- ASpli::aspliExampleBamList()
targets <- data.frame( 
  row.names = paste0('Sample',c(1:12)),
  bam = BAMFiles,
  f1 = rep("A",12),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
genomeTxDb <- txdbmaker::makeTxDbFromGFF(gtfFileName)
features <- binGenome(genomeTxDb, logTo = NULL)
ASpliSE <- BamtoAspliCounts(
                    features = features,
                    targets = targets,
                    minReadLength = 100,
                    libType = "SE",
                    BPPARAM = MulticoreParam(1L)
                    )
SEbins <- convertASpli(ASpliSE, type = "bin")
SEjunctions <- convertASpli(ASpliSE, type = "junction")
metadata(SEbins)$design <- ~1
metadata(SEjunctions)$design <- ~1
SEbins <- calculateOffsets(SEbins, 
                            method = "AS", 
                            aggregation = "locus")
SEjunctions <- calculateOffsets(SEjunctions, 
                            method = "AS", 
                            aggregation = "symbol",
                            mergeGeneASpli = TRUE)
filterbins <- filterByExpr(SEbins)
SEbins <- SEbins[filterbins,]
filterjunctions <- filterByExpr(SEjunctions)
SEjunctions <- SEjunctions[filterjunctions,]
SEbins <- saseRfindEncodingDim(SEbins, method = "GD")
SEjunctions <- saseRfindEncodingDim(SEjunctions, method = "GD")
SEbins <- saseRfit(SEbins,
                    analysis = "AS",
                    padjust = "BH",
                    fit = "fast")
SEjunctions <- saseRfit(SEjunctions,
                    analysis = "AS",
                    padjust = "BH",
                    fit = "fast")

workflows.name: differential_usage_analysis_with_adapted_offsets
workflows.intent: Perform differential usage/splicing analysis using adapted offsets in DESeq2 or edgeR.
workflows.stages: 1. Convert GTF to TxDb and extract exonic parts using exonicParts ;; 2. Count overlaps using summarizeOverlaps ;; 3. Define experimental conditions in colData ;; 4. Aggregate counts per gene to calculate gene-level offsets ;; 5. Adjust zero offsets and counts to 1 ;; 6. Run DESeq2 or edgeR with the custom offsets
workflows.code:
gtfFileName <- aspliExampleGTF()
BAMFiles <- aspliExampleBamList()
genomeTxDb <- txdbmaker::makeTxDbFromGFF(gtfFileName)
flattenedAnnotation = GenomicFeatures::exonicParts(genomeTxDb, 
                                  linked.to.single.gene.only=TRUE )
se = GenomicAlignments::summarizeOverlaps(
    flattenedAnnotation,
    BAMFiles, 
    singleEnd=TRUE, 
    ignore.strand=TRUE )
colData(se)$condition <- factor(c(rep(c("control", "case"), each = 6)))
counts <- assays(se)$counts
offsetsGene <- aggregate(counts,
                     by = list("gene" = rowData(se)$gene_id), FUN = sum) 
offsets <- offsetsGene[match(rowData(se)$gene_id, offsetsGene$gene), ] %>% 
                     mutate("gene" = NULL) %>% 
                     as.matrix() 
index <- offsets == 0
counts[index] <- 1
offsets[index] <- 1
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts,
                              colData = colData(se),
                              rowData = rowData(se),
                              design= ~ condition)
normalizationFactors(dds) <- offsets
dds <- DESeq2::estimateDispersionsGeneEst(dds)
dispersions(dds) <- mcols(dds)$dispGeneEst
dds <- DESeq2::nbinomWaldTest(dds)
results_dds <- DESeq2::results(dds)
DGE <- DGEList(counts = counts)
DGE$offset <- log(offsets)
design <- model.matrix(~condition, data = colData(se))
DGE <- edgeR::estimateDisp(DGE, design = design)
fitDGE <- edgeR::glmFit(DGE, design= design)
results_DGE <- edgeR::glmLRT(fitDGE, coef = 2)
